I have been wondering a lot about people who want only conference champions to be selected for the Playoff so I put together this to determine if that was a minority or majority opinion.

Its December 2015, you are a committee member to select the playoffs for the upcoming championship. The following information is all you have to make your selections.

The conference champions are:
Ohio State 11-2 (big 10) SOS 42nd.
Georgia 12-1 (sec) SOS 10th.
Stanford 11-2 (pac12) SOS 37th.
Baylor 12-1 (Big 12 SOS 88th.
Clemson 11-2 (ACC) SOS 25th.

However, Arizona State went into the Pac12 championship undefeated and got beaten by Stanford and is now 12-1 and Arkansas went into the SEC championship undefeated and was beaten by Georgia and now is also 12-1.

How would you vote? Would be #1, #2, #3, and #4 in your opinions?
Hypothetical playoff scenario - You are the Committee.

I think you have to also take into consideration the SOS of Arizona State and Arkansas if they are to be considered. I'm not sure where you got your SOS rankings, but I used ESPN's 2015 FPI.

By these metrics, the conference champions are:

  • Ohio State 11-2 (big 10) SOS 49th.
  • Georgia 12-1 (sec) SOS 18th.
  • Stanford 11-2 (pac12) SOS 8th.
  • Baylor 12-1 (big 12) SOS 50th.
  • Clemson 11-2 (acc) SOS 36th.

Arizona State 12-1 (pac12) SOS 22nd.

Arkansas 12-1 (sec) SOS 3rd.

The problem with these numbers is that they are preseason SOS rankings, but assuming they don't vary too much, here's how I would rank the top 4.

  1. Georgia 12-1 (sec) SOS 18th - Georgia gets number one for winning the SEC with a 1-loss record combined with a top 20 SOS.
  2. Stanford - 11-2 (pac12) SOS 8th - Stanford is in at number 2 because of winning their conference, their record, and their SOS
  3. Arkansas - 12-1 (sec) SOS 3rd - Arkansas goes third rather than second because of a top 5 SOS. The CFP does not want to see another SEC v. SEC national championship (at least not in this scenario).
  4. Baylor - 12-1 (big 12) SOS 50th - Baylor gets in over Ohio State because of their record.

I don't think Arizona State gets in simply because they didn't win their conference combined with their lower SOS.
So people with better records are left out because they lost one game, the championship game?

In this specific scenarios, yes. College football is a "what have you done for me lately" sport and I think winning a conference championship is a statement game. Stanford with the 8th toughest SOS and winning their conference championship over Arizona State (22nd SOS) deserves to be in the playoffs in my opinion. Granted, the only metrics we're looking at here are SOS and W-L records.

I had this thought earlier today, and I thought to share. In "On the Run" we see Pearl and Amethyst fight for (I think) the only time in the entire series. Pearl briefly toys with her, before asserting that Amethyst can't win. Then Amethyst pulls out a double whip electro power move (patent pending) that throws Pearl back, and then breaks down into tears, along with the audience. I think it's a safe assumption to make that Pearl is the stronger of the two gems, a claim that Amethyst didn't refute (she just didn't care). What does this mean?

Well, we recently got confirmation that Pearl isn't like Garnet or Amethyst, she's a gem with a purpose, and apparently useless on her own. Beyond that, she said in "Sworn to the Sword" that she wasn't built for fighting. This all ties in nicely with the "Pearls are a servant class" theory that has a lot of traction in the fandom. Conversely, Amethyst was made in the Kindergarten. Amethyst was made for a purpose too, but we don't know it yet. I don't think it's a stretch to say she was supposed to be a soldier, but got "overcooked" and left behind.

Putting two and two together, Pearl, a gem that isn't built for fighting, is stronger than Amethyst, a gem that, arguably, was. Amethyst must be uniquely weak when compared to other gems. Even in other battles, like against Lapis and Steven's watermelon's, Amethyst gets soundly beaten.

Whatever "overcooked" means for Amethyst, it seems that it weakened her immensely when compared to what she could have been.
It's possible that being a younger gem her lack of experience hinders her as well. Also, she might not necessarily be inherently weaker, but handicapped by her lack of discipline.

I think that when she went into the double whip electro power move might have been the tip of the iceberg, for now I think her real power needs to be awakened by anger, until she learns to control it that is.
